b1.summary: Two failure modes. (a) T3 security miss: every model put one generic 'bytes>0 && data==nullptr' guard at Invoke (or eval-phase accessors) and never fixed reshape Prepare, which calls IsConstantTensor(GetInput(...kShapeTensor)) on the nullptr returned for an absent (-1) input -> SIGSEGV in 7 of 8 counted runs. (b) T2 coupled keep-working value: the blanket guard refuses a RESHAPE whose rank-2 second input is unread and buffer-less (5 of 8 runs; sole cause of DS run 1). Not counted: mimo 2026-10-23T13:21 (timed out at 2 h, unaudited, re-run) and mimo 2026-10-25T07:51 (ungraded). The counted mimo 04:48 run timed out (3 h) but was graded and audited.

b2.note: Only 2 tests decide all 8 runs: Reshape_OmittedShapeInput fails in 7/8, IgnoredSecondInput in 5/8. DS's 0/3 rests on the functional test in run 1 and on both in runs 2-3; mimo's last three runs rest on the single security test.

b3.note: Near misses (one failing test from 1.0): DS 13:09 (functional only) and mimo 00:12, 02:43, 04:48 (security only).

b4.note: Every run uses the same generic Invoke-time guard; all 8 miss the setup-time absent-input route except DS run 1, which hit only the over-refusal. Early mimo/DS runs also over-refuse the unread rank-2 input; later mimo runs (accessor-gated eval flag) avoid it but still miss T3.

b5.open_human_question: FAIRNESS.md (2026-10-23): confirm that a setup-time (AllocateTensors/Prepare) refusal of a not-yet-filled graph input is an over-broad, wrong fix, so FunctionalSuite.ExpandDims_Normal and ProjectKernelTests are fair, given the instruction says 'Running or setting up a graph'. No resolution recorded. It does not touch any counted run's decisive tests (those two tests failed only in the uncounted timed-out mimo 13:21 run). The 'Required: generalize' instruction rewrites were never applied (instruction.md dated 2026-10-23 04:23, before the review).

b6.reason: The decisive security trap T3 (absent -1 shape input dereferenced in reshape Prepare) is not covered: upstream_fix.patch (0b5662bc + f8378920) only adds the Invoke-time loop check and scores 0.8 on the gate, failing exactly Reshape_OmittedShapeInput (notes.md: still in master on 2026-10-23). It decides 7 of 8 runs. The keep-working value (unread rank-2 second input exempt) IS the published fix B's narrowed exemption (dims->size != 1), so a model that looks up the fix avoids that regression. It alone decided DS run 1.

quotes: A node input that is declared but absent must likewise never be dereferenced: the node must either proceed without it, when the operator can, or refuse cleanly.
Running or setting up a graph must never read through a tensor that carries no data.
An input that an operator never reads may be left without data; a model that does this keeps running exactly as today.
whatever the operator involved and however the graph was produced or supplied to the runtime
Fix the problem and its close variants.
b7.note: listing.json marks all 3 traps DESCRIBED. The fairness review flagged items 1-3 as 'Required: generalize' because each sentence exists for one trap (T3, the setup stage, T2's coupled value). None was applied. Both decisive traps are stated almost literally, and models still failed.

b8.blind: not run (blind_status.txt: 'error 3: could not extract /app from cwe-blind-src:stk-tensorflow-ghsajjr8')
b8.note: Oracle 1.0 x3. Two other correctly shaped fixes pass: alt_kernel_checks.patch (per-kernel guards) 1.0 and hardening.patch 1.0. Wrong-fix checks behave as expected (upstream_fix 0.8, upstream_first_fix 0.6, overbroad_refuse 0.0).

c1.mechanism: null pointer dereference: a model-supplied tensor with no data buffer, or an absent (-1) node input, is dereferenced
c1.domain: ML inference runtime (TensorFlow Lite interpreter, model loading)

c2.note: Secondary trap: keep-working-value 'over-blocked legitimate use (unread input without data)', which is covered upstream by fix B. Build score flagged single-trap-carries: T1 is medium tier, so the difficulty rests on T2 and T3.

e2.why: All 8 counted failing runs audited trustworthy, model-failed, high confidence.

e3.why: Gate A is READY but NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES is still open (setup-time refusal question), and the required instruction generalisation was not applied. The open question is not decisive for any counted run.

e4.why: Reshape_OmittedShapeInput (SIGSEGV, a hole left open) decides 7 of 8 runs.

e5.why: The published A+B fix leaves T3 open; the gate's upstream_fix.patch fails exactly that test.

concerns: Fragile: 2 tests decide everything, and one security test (Reshape_OmittedShapeInput) carries 7/8 runs. 4 of 8 runs were one test short of 1.0.

Leaky instruction: the T3 and T2 sentences describe the traps nearly literally (listing: all DESCRIBED). The fairness review's 'Required: generalize' rewrites were never applied, so a rewrite could change difficulty in either direction.
DS run 1 was decided only by a keep-working regression that the public fix B covers, so DS's 0/3 partly rests on a covered value.
An open human-review flag in FAIRNESS.md has no recorded resolution (not decisive for counted runs).
The blind fix was never produced (extract error), so the only solvability evidence is builder-written patches.
Security harness leniency: RunOrRefuse ignores status, so a signal handler or dummy buffer would pass (fairness section 2). The breaker is not affected, but test quality is weak.
Mimo needed 7 attempts: 1 timed out at 2 h and was unaudited, 1 ungraded. One counted run hit the 3 h timeout (counted as a fail by project rule).
